title: Everything Links
briefing: Launch day for a link shortener. Traffic climbs from 1,000 to 3,000 requests per second over the first 30 seconds and stays there.
Every request needs 5ms of CPU on an app server, then one trip to the database: 95% look up a short link to redirect it, the rest create a new one.
This is your first database: one machine that every request needs. It does a fixed number of reads a second, and a write costs more than a read.
At some point during the run, one of your app servers will crash.
debrief: The app tier is pages 1 to 3: 15 vCPUs of work on six medium servers is 63% busy, 75% after the crash, with retries covering it.
The database is new: 2,850 reads plus 150 writes at 2.5 reads each is 3,225 reads' worth, 65% of a medium one and 129% of a small one.
Same 70% rule, different machine. In an interview, say how you make short codes: a counter in base 62 never collides.

solutions.name: Six medium servers and a medium database
solutions.explanation: 24 vCPUs for 15 vCPUs of work: 63% busy, and 75% after the crash. Retries cover the dead server. The medium database is 65% busy with every redirect and every new link.

solutions.name: Four large servers and a medium database
solutions.explanation: More headroom on the app tier: 47% busy, 63% after the crash, for $240 a month more. The database is the same medium one, 65% busy.

antiSolutions.name: A small database
antiSolutions.explanation: The app tier is fine, but 3,225 reads' worth of work a second is 129% of a small database. It falls behind from the peak on, and requests time out waiting for it.

antiSolutions.name: No retries
antiSolutions.explanation: A spare server, but no retry at the load balancer. With the default 30-second health checks, a quarter of all requests go to the dead server for almost a minute.

antiSolutions.name: No spare server
antiSolutions.explanation: Three large servers carry the peak at 63% until one crashes. Then two of them do 15 vCPUs of work on 16 vCPUs, 94% busy, and p99 climbs past the limit.

antiSolutions.name: A large database
antiSolutions.explanation: It works, at 32% busy, but it costs twice a medium one: $1,585 a month against $1,300.
